# Search In Sorted Matrix

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-medium-yellow)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

Given an n×m matrix where each row and each column is sorted in ascending order, and a target value, return the [row, col] position of the target. Return [-1, -1] if the target is not present.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                                           | Time     | Space |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----- |
| Solution1 | Row-by-row linear scan with early break            | O(n·m)   | O(1)  |
| Solution2 | Start top-right, eliminate row or column each step | O(n + m) | O(1)  |

# Breadth First Search

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-medium-yellow)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

Given a node in a directed acyclic graph where each node has a name and a list of children, traverse the graph in breadth-first order and return a list of node names in the order they are visited. The traversal starts from the node on which the method is called.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                  | Time     | Space |
| --------- | ------------------------- | -------- | ----- |
| Solution1 | BFS with ArrayDeque       | O(v + e) | O(v)  |
| Solution2 | BFS with LinkedList Queue | O(v + e) | O(v)  |

# Binary Search

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-warm--up-green)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

A sorted array of distinct integers and a target value are provided; return the index of the target in the array, or -1 if it is absent. The array is guaranteed to be sorted in ascending order, so a logarithmic-time approach is possible. Negative integers may appear among the elements.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                   | Time     | Space    |
| --------- | -------------------------- | -------- | -------- |
| Solution1 | Iterative binary search    | O(log n) | O(1)     |
| Solution2 | Iterative, compareTo-based | O(log n) | O(1)     |
| Solution3 | Recursive binary search    | O(log n) | O(log n) |

# Search For Range

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-hard-orange)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

Given a sorted array of integers that may contain duplicates and a target value, find the first and last index at which the target appears. If the target is not in the array, return [-1, -1]. The solution must run in O(log n).

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                                              | Time     | Space    |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- |
| Solution1 | Two binary searches (iterative) biased left and right | O(log n) | O(1)     |
| Solution2 | Two binary searches (recursive) biased left and right | O(log n) | O(log n) |

# Depth First Search

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-warm--up-green)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

A named graph node is provided where each node holds a string name and a list of child nodes; traverse the graph depth-first and return a list of node names in the order they were visited. The graph is a directed acyclic tree rooted at the node on which the method is called. Children of each node should be visited left to right.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                             | Time     | Space |
| --------- | ------------------------------------ | -------- | ----- |
| Solution1 | Recursive DFS, pre-order             | O(v + e) | O(v)  |
| Solution2 | Recursive DFS via stack accumulation | O(v + e) | O(v)  |
| Solution3 | Iterative DFS with explicit stack    | O(v + e) | O(v)  |

# Shifted Binary Search

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-hard-orange)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

Given a sorted array of distinct integers that has been rotated at an unknown pivot point, search for a target value and return its index. If the target is absent, return -1. The algorithm must run in O(log n).

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                                          | Time     | Space |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----- |
| Solution1 | Modified binary search distinguishing sorted half | O(log n) | O(1)  |

# Multi String Search

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-hard-orange)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

Given a large text string and an array of search keys, determine for each key whether it appears as a substring of the text. Return a list of booleans in the same order as the keys.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                                       | Time | Space |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---- | ----- | ----- | --- | --- | --- | ---- | --- |
| Solution1 | Suffix trie of text + membership check per key | O(   | text  | ² + Σ | key | )   | O(  | text | ²)  |

# Circle Of Numbers

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-warm--up-green)
**Source:** CodeSignal

## 1. Problem

Given n numbers arranged in a circle, find the number that sits exactly opposite to a given starting position (i.e., n/2 positions away).

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                   | Time | Space |
| --------- | -------------------------- | ---- | ----- |
| Solution1 | Direct arithmetic modulo n | O(1) | O(1)  |

# Valid Starting City

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-medium-yellow)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

Given arrays of city-to-city distances and fuel amounts at each city, and a fuel efficiency value (miles per gallon), find the index of the one valid starting city from which a car can complete a full circular trip visiting every city in order without running out of fuel.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                                      | Time  | Space |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----- |
| Solution1 | Try each city as start, simulate full circuit | O(n²) | O(1)  |

# Circle Of Numbers

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-easy-yellowgreen)
**Source:** CodeSignal

## 1. Problem

Numbers 0 through n-1 are placed at equal intervals around a circle. Given n (even) and a starting position firstNumber, return the number directly opposite to it — i.e., the one exactly n/2 steps away.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                                      | Time | Space |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---- | ----- |
| Solution1 | Modular arithmetic: (firstNumber + n/2) mod n | O(1) | O(1)  |

# Optimal Freelancing

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-warm--up-green)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

An array of freelance jobs is provided, each with a payment amount and a deadline (number of days, max 7) by which it must be completed in a single day; select a subset of jobs to maximise total payment given that only one job can be done per day and all work must be scheduled within a 7-day window. Return the maximum achievable payment. Deadlines beyond 7 are treated as day 7.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                              | Time       | Space |
| --------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------- | ----- |
| Solution1 | Greedy max-heap, schedule latest slot | O(n log n) | O(n)  |

# Caesar Cipher Encryptor

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-warm--up-green)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

Shift every lowercase letter in a string forward by a given integer key, wrapping around the alphabet, and return the resulting ciphertext string. The input contains only lowercase English letters, and the shift key may be larger than 26. Each character is shifted independently using modular arithmetic.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                        | Time | Space |
| --------- | ------------------------------- | ---- | ----- |
| Solution1 | Alphabet string indexOf lookup  | O(n) | O(n)  |
| Solution2 | Arithmetic modulo 26, char cast | O(n) | O(n)  |
| Solution3 | Arithmetic modulo 26            | O(n) | O(n)  |

# Nth Fibonacci

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-warm--up-green)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

An integer n is provided; return the nth number in the Fibonacci sequence, where F(1) = 0, F(2) = 1, and each subsequent term is the sum of the two preceding ones. n is at least 1. The sequence is 1-indexed, so F(1) = 0 and F(3) = 1.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                               | Time   | Space |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | ------ | ----- |
| Solution1 | Naive recursion                        | O(2^n) | O(n)  |
| Solution2 | Recursive memoization, HashMap         | O(n)   | O(n)  |
| Solution3 | Recursive memoization, array           | O(n)   | O(n)  |
| Solution4 | Iterative, two-variable rolling window | O(n)   | O(1)  |

# Find Email Domain

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-warm--up-green)
**Source:** CodeSignal

## 1. Problem

Given an email address, extract and return the domain (everything after the last '@' character).

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                        | Time | Space |
| --------- | ------------------------------- | ---- | ----- |
| Solution1 | lastIndexOf('@') then substring | O(n) | O(n)  |

# Shortest Unique Prefixes

![Difficulty](https://img.shields.io/badge/difficulty-hard-orange)
**Source:** AlgoExpert

## 1. Problem

Given an array of distinct strings, find for each string the shortest prefix that uniquely identifies it among all strings in the array. Return the prefixes in the same order as the input strings.

## 2. Solutions

| File      | Approach                                     | Time   | Space  |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------ | ------ |
| Solution1 | Trie with per-node child-count + prefix walk | O(n·m) | O(n·m) |

name: github-pages
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false
env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
        with:
          enablement: true
      - uses: actions/jekyll-build-pages@v1
        with:
          source: ./
          destination: ./_site
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

name: java-build
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"
          cache: maven
      - name: Compile, test, and verify invariants
        run: bash scripts/verify_final.sh
      - name: Trunk Check
        uses: trunk-io/trunk-action@v1

[project]
name = "tech-interview-questions-python"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Python ports of selected interview-prep problem solutions"
requires-python = ">=3.10"

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
pythonpath = ["src"]

# Tech Interview Questions

[![build](https://github.com/thekaveh/tech-interview-questions/actions/workflows/java-build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thekaveh/tech-interview-questions/actions/workflows/java-build.yml)

A personal collection of solved coding-interview problems from AlgoExpert,
CodeSignal, and Educative. Solutions are my own work; problem statements in
each `README.md` are paraphrased in my own words.

## 1. Browse problems

Open the [online problem catalog](https://thekaveh.github.io/tech-interview-questions/PROBLEMS.html)
or the [problem index](PROBLEMS.md). Choose a provider and tier, then open a
problem to read its paraphrased statement and compare solution approaches with
their time and space complexity.

For a first example, read [Two Number Sum](java/src/main/java/algoexpert/easy/two_number_sum/README.md).
Its table compares brute force, sorting with binary search, and two pointers.
Open its [Java implementations](https://github.com/thekaveh/tech-interview-questions/tree/main/java/src/main/java/algoexpert/easy/two_number_sum)
to study each approach. Browsing
requires no local build; the Python tree currently contains one example port.

## 2. Build locally

Install Git, a JDK **17 or newer**, and Maven before running the commands below.
Make sure `java` and `mvn` are available in your shell. From a new checkout:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/thekaveh/tech-interview-questions.git
cd tech-interview-questions
```

From the checkout root, build the Java project:

```bash
(cd java && mvn -B verify)
```

A successful run ends with Maven's `BUILD SUCCESS`. It compiles every Java
solution and runs the JUnit smoke test that loads each `Solution{N}` class through
reflection. This checks compilation and class loading, not the correctness of
every algorithm. See the [Python guide](python/README.md) for its separate test path.

## 3. Inventory

| Provider   | Problems | Solutions |
| ---------- | -------: | --------: |
| AlgoExpert |      168 |       316 |
| CodeSignal |      102 |       150 |
| Educative  |        8 |         9 |
| **Total**  |  **278** |   **475** |

## 4. Layout

```text
java/                              ← Java solutions (active)
  src/main/java/
    algoexpert/{easy,medium,hard,veryhard}/<problem>/
    codesignal/{intro,thecore}/<problem>/
    educative/patterns/<pattern>/<problem>/
python/                            ← stub for future Python ports
scripts/                           ← end-state verification + index generator
```

Each `<problem>/` directory contains a `README.md` (problem summary,
difficulty badge, complexity table) and one or more `SolutionN.java`
files where the number denotes attempt order.

## 5. Difficulty badges

- ![warmup](https://img.shields.io/badge/-warm--up-green) — elementary, FizzBuzz-tier
- ![easy](https://img.shields.io/badge/-easy-yellowgreen)
- ![medium](https://img.shields.io/badge/-medium-yellow)
- ![hard](https://img.shields.io/badge/-hard-orange)
- ![very-hard](https://img.shields.io/badge/-very--hard-red)

The badge defaults from the source tier but is labeled honestly per
problem — some "easy"-tier problems are really warm-ups.

## 6. Extend the collection

External contributions are not actively solicited. Forks and future additions
should follow the public [contributor and style guide](https://github.com/thekaveh/tech-interview-questions/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md),
which covers layout, solution naming, code style, catalog regeneration and checks.

## 7. License

[MIT license](https://github.com/thekaveh/tech-interview-questions/blob/main/LICENSE)

# Python solutions

Stub tree for future Python ports of selected problems. Mirrors the
`java/` layout: `src/<provider>/<tier>/<problem_snake>/solution_<N>.py`.

Currently a single example (Two Number Sum) is here to prove the layout
and test wiring work. Add more as desired; each new problem follows the
public [solution-shape conventions](https://github.com/thekaveh/tech-interview-questions/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#1-layout-and-solution-shape),
translated to Python idioms.

## 1. Layout

```text
python/
  pyproject.toml
  src/<provider>/<tier>/<problem_snake>/solution_<N>.py
  tests/<provider>/<tier>/<problem_snake>/test_solution_<N>.py
```

## 2. Running the tests

Install Python 3.10+ before testing. From the repository root, create an isolated
environment and install `pytest`, then enter the Python project:

```bash
python3 -m venv /tmp/tech-interview-python-venv
. /tmp/tech-interview-python-venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install pytest
cd python
python3 -m pytest
```

The current example's tests should pass. These tests cover the single Python port,
not the Java collection.

## 3. Conventions

- One module per solution attempt, named `solution_1.py`,
  `solution_2.py`, …
- Module exposes a top-level function whose name matches the problem
  verb (e.g. `two_number_sum(...)`).
- One `# Approach: ...` comment at the top of each solution module,
  matching the Java tree's convention.
- Tests in `tests/` mirror the source tree; each `test_solution_<N>.py`
  imports the matching solution module and asserts the canonical
  example.
